record.original_question: Can every catalytic logspace computation be simulated in polynomial time; equivalently, is CL ⊆ P?

evidence.quote: Definition 3. The class CL is defined as CSPACE(O(log n), nO(1)).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a deterministic Turing machine equipped with three tapes: a read-only input tape, a read-write work tape, and a read-write auxiliary tape called the catalytic tape. The catalytic tape is initialized with an arbitrary string $\tau \in \{0,1\}^{s_c(n)}$ (the "catalyst"), and $M$ may read and write its cells freely during the computation, but is required to restore the catalytic tape to its initial content $\tau$ upon halting, for every input $x$ of length $n$ and every choice of $\tau$. We say $M$ uses work space $s_w(n)$ and catalytic space $s_c(n)$ if on every input of length $n$ and every initial catalyst, $M$ uses at most $s_w(n)$ cells of the work tape and the catalytic tape has length $s_c(n)$. The class $\mathrm{CSPACE}(s_w(n), s_c(n))$ consists of all languages decided by such machines with work space $O(s_w(n))$ and catalytic space $O(s_c(n))$, with the correctness and restoration conditions holding for every catalyst $\tau$. Define
$$\mathrm{CL} \;=\; \mathrm{CSPACE}\bigl(O(\log n),\; n^{O(1)}\bigr).$$
Let $\mathrm{P}$ denote the class of languages decidable by a deterministic Turing machine in time $n^{O(1)}$.

Question: Is $\mathrm{CL} \subseteq \mathrm{P}$? Equivalently, can every catalytic logspace computation (using polynomial-length catalytic tape) be simulated by some deterministic algorithm running in polynomial time?
artifact.status_search_result: The containment CL ⊆ P remains a central open problem in catalytic complexity. The best known upper bound places CL inside TC¹, and recent works (2025) have shown specific problems such as bipartite matching and linear matroid intersection lie in the subclass CLP = CL ∩ P, but the general question whether all of CL fits in P is still open.

status_evidence.title: Linear Matroid Intersection is in Catalytic Logspace
status_evidence.snippet: Understanding CL remains a major open problem, with TC^1 as the best known upper bound.
status_evidence.claim: CL ⊆ P is unresolved; the best known containment is CL ⊆ TC^1.

status_evidence.title: Bipartite Matching is in Catalytic Logspace
status_evidence.snippet: Bipartite maximum matching can be computed in CLP ⊆ P; first problem outside TC^1 shown to be in CL.
status_evidence.claim: Recent results place specific problems in CLP = CL ∩ P, but do not resolve CL ⊆ P.

status_evidence.title: The Structure of Catalytic Space: Capturing ...
status_evidence.snippet: CL ∩ P = CLP; showing CL ⊆ P is equivalent to making catalytic algorithms run in worst-case polynomial time.
status_evidence.claim: The problem CL ⊆ P is equivalent to CL = CLP and remains open.
